source.title: Munda Politics and Land: Understanding Indigeneity in Jharkhand, India
source.author: Pallavi Raonka

exact_locators.support: 15-month ethnographic study, May 2017–December 2018, concerning Munda community meanings of land and Adivasi-State conflict
expedited IRB approval granted June 27 2017; approval to audio-record interviews of activists working with Munda communities
project described as ethnographic study of Munda everyday life and land/forest meanings
chapter described as based on oral-history interviews with Pathalgarhi leaders/participants plus participant observation and village visits
author explains an interview was not camera/audio-recorded because recording could make the participant uncomfortable under surveillance

geography: Khunti and other field sites as documented in dissertation
scope.caution: Treat author observations, participant statements, and cited-literature synthesis as distinct evidence classes. Do not universalize local/field observations to all Munda communities.

governance.sensitive_participant_material: Do not expose participant-linked interview/photographic material until consent and cultural-access review is complete.
governance.promotion_policy: Metadata/method locators may support source provenance. Cultural propositions remain candidate-only until proposition atomization, dependency, rights, consent and cultural-access review.
